reviewer: build-lane worker (code-grounded + live probe + acceptance validator), revision 1

rubric.evidence: Real transformers.js token-classification in a dedicated module Worker (models/camembert-ner/worker.js): loadPipeline({task:"token-classification", model:"Xenova/camembert-ner", backend:"wasm", dtype:"q8"}) then pipe(text) for per-sub-token {entity,score,index,word}. Verified by a pre-build live probe in headless Chrome (transformers.js 3.7.5, exact shared CDN build): 'Apple est créée par Steve Jobs à Los Altos en Californie.' → I-ORG 'Apple' 0.85, I-PER 'Steve/Job/s' 0.96–0.99, I-LOC 'Los/Al/tos' + 'Californie' — real q8 WASM output, never canned. CamemBERT is SentencePiece with an I-only tag set ({O,I-PER,I-ORG,I-LOC,I-MISC}), so the worker merges sub-word pieces into words (▁-boundary + monotonic char-cursor walk), maps each word to its char span, and aggregates consecutive same-type words into entity spans (WikiNER simple aggregation).
rubric.notes: Raw sub-tokens, merged words AND entity spans are all returned so the page shows the genuine token→word→span reconstruction.

rubric.evidence: Pipeline output is per-token {entity, score, index, word}; worker post-processes to per-word {surface, entity, type, score, start, end} and per-span {type, text, start, end, score}. The I-only label set means spans come from consecutive same-type words — 'Los' I-LOC + 'Al' I-LOC + 'tos' I-LOC → one LOC 'Los Altos' (probe-verified token stream). Shape matches the token-classification pipeline contract and the model card's aggregation_strategy=simple example.
rubric.notes: Char-span mapping makes inline highlighting and redaction land exactly on the original text (the pipeline returns no offsets).

rubric.evidence: At-a-glance declares the exact loaded repo (Xenova/camembert-ner, linked) as the ONNX q8 export of Jean-Baptiste/camembert-ner (linked), task token-classification, WikiNER tag set, architecture (CamemBERT RoBERTa SentencePiece ~110M, fine-tuned on ~170k WikiNER-fr sentences), language French (honest note + links to the built English bert-ner and multilingual-ner families), q8 quantisation, WebAssembly backend (no WebGPU), ~111 MB download, MIT license. Matches worker.js + every createModelLoader call site (literal modelId, dtype q8, sizeMB 111).
rubric.notes: hfId records the repo actually loaded (Xenova conversion), matching the bert-ner/pos-tagging precedent; the canonical Jean-Baptiste repo is linked and credited.

rubric.evidence: Every route loads via shared createModelLoader (literal modelId "Xenova/camembert-ner"; multi-model adds "Xenova/camembert-base"). A valid cached model auto-initialises with no Load click; Download/Re-download/Update + clear-cache appear otherwise. The acceptance validator reuses one Chrome profile across route cells, so later routes prove cached auto-init after the first real download.
rubric.notes: modelId keyed on the repo so the ~111 MB cache is tracked for the no-silent-re-download guarantee.

role=status aria-live status + aria-live output; each entity chip carries a text type label (never colour alone) plus a title with raw label + confidence; every button/input/select has an accessible name (validator asserts); recast inputs get per-entity aria-labels; palette tuned for light+dark WCAG AA (same palette discipline as pos-tagging).

rubric.evidence: Fluid flex/grid with flex-wrap, intrinsic sizing and logical properties; no fixed widths; textarea min-block-size; chips wrap. Acceptance validator drives 1280×800 desktop AND 360×740 mobile (DPR 3, touch) on all five routes and asserts scrollWidth−innerWidth ≤ 1; responsive-check runs the same matrix.

All inference AND the sub-word merge/char-span mapping/span aggregation run in a module Worker; the main thread only renders. Typing is debounced (350ms) so WASM runs don't queue per keystroke. No dense-output canvas composite (text-only family).

openQuestions: The tag set is I-only (no B- tags), so two ADJACENT same-type entities with no separator merge into one span ('simple' aggregation, same as the model card). Worth noting if a user pastes 'Paris Lyon' expecting two locations.
The model is FRENCH — is the language note prominent enough that an English-speaking visitor isn't surprised? (Mirrors the pos-tagging family's honest-note pattern.)

followUpGoals.goal: Add lang="fr" to the French text regions for correct screen-reader pronunciation of highlighted entities.
Batch mode: entity-index several documents in one run via the worker's tagMany path (already implemented worker-side).
